aria: Animated recap of the Lakers' 123 to 112 road win at Milwaukee: Luka Dončić's driving floater with a second left in the third quarter that made it 94 to 73, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 32 points, the top scorers, how the Lakers won, and the next game at Phoenix.
notes: Box score from the Lakers' 123–112 road win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Nov 11, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the AP (via WMTV), Field Level Media, Fadeaway World (via Yahoo Sports), Basketnews and the CBS Sports play-by-play. All 123 Lakers points and all 112 Bucks points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (61–50 at the half, 94–73 after three; AP, Field Level Media). Biggest leads: the Lakers' 24 and Milwaukee's 5 (Covers.com); the Lakers led by 24 with 4:25 left (Field Level Media). Team stats (fast-break points, points in the paint, steals) are from Covers.com. Records and conference ranks are from the site's standings (data/season.json) after Wednesday's games: the Lakers 11–2 (first in the west), Phoenix 4–6.

It was the Lakers' seventh straight win and Milwaukee's eighth straight loss; the Lakers have won four of their last five visits to Milwaukee and made 7 of 11 threes in the third quarter (Field Level Media). Dončić scored 16 in the first quarter on 5-of-9 shooting (Field Level Media). He was holding his right ankle after a shot while fouled by Kyle Kuzma late in the fourth, made the free throw and came out with 4:25 left; JJ Redick called it a light tweak (Field Level Media; Basketnews). Austin Reaves left in the third with a left heel injury (Field Level Media). The Lakers play at Phoenix on Sunday at 4:00 PM ET (AP; Sportbusy schedule).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Luka Dončić's driving floating bank shot, assisted by Jarred Vanderbilt, with one second left in the third quarter, which made it 94–73 (CBS Sports play-by-play; the AP and Field Level Media have the 94–73 score after three). It is drawn as a basket on a drive from 92–73; the bank finish itself isn't animated. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Los Angeles Lakers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Dončić’s listed 6-foot-8 and 230 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to his reported 6-foot-11 wingspan (NBA Draft Room), in the Lakers' road kit with his look from the site's looks file. His No. 77 is from Basketball-Reference. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
